\subsection*{RAMSimulation --- Word Size: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.RAMSimulation.WordSize}.

\subsection*{RAMSimulation --- Word Size: Results}

\begin{definition}[Computability with word and space bounds]
\lean{WordRAM.WordSizeComputable}
\label{WordRAM.WordSizeComputable}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed}
Let $W,TW,SW$ be functions from natural numbers to natural numbers. There is a Turing
machine with a finite Boolean tape alphabet such that, for every finite Boolean input
list $x$, it outputs the binary representation of $W(|x|)$ within some time $t\le
TW(|x|)$, and uses at most $SW(|x|)$ cells of space during those $t$ steps.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of time and space bounds]
\lean{WordRAM.WordSizeComputable.mono}
\label{WordRAM.WordSizeComputable.mono}
\leanok
\uses{WordRAM.WordSizeComputable}
Suppose a word-size function $W$ is computable by a finite Turing machine within time
bound $T(n)$ and space bound $S(n)$: on every Boolean input $x$, the machine produces
the bit representation of $W(|x|)$ after some $t\le T(|x|)$ steps and uses at most
$S(|x|)$ work-tape cells. If $T(n)\le T'(n)$ and $S(n)\le S'(n)$ for every $n\in\mathbb
N$, then $W$ is computable within time bound $T'$ and space bound $S'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Logarithmic-space word-size computation]
\lean{WordRAM.wordSizeComputable_logSpace}
\label{WordRAM.wordSizeComputable_logSpace}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.logSpace, WordRAM.WordSizeComputable}
For every natural number $c$, there is a natural number $a$ and a finite Turing machine
over the Boolean alphabet such that, on every Boolean input $x$ of length $n$, the
machine outputs the binary bits of $c(\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1)$ within at most $a(n+1)$
steps and uses at most $a(\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1)$ work-tape cells.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Computing a scaled space-constructible function]
\lean{WordRAM.wordSizeComputable_of_spaceConstructible}
\label{WordRAM.wordSizeComputable_of_spaceConstructible}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SpaceConstructible, WordRAM.WordSizeComputable}
Let $S:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be space constructible, and let $c\in\mathbb{N}$. Then
there exist $a\in\mathbb{N}$ and a time bound $TW:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that a
finite Boolean Turing machine, on every Boolean input $x$, outputs the binary
representation of $cS(|x|)$ within $TW(|x|)$ steps and uses at most $aS(|x|)$ work-tape
cells.
\end{theorem}
